name: Crackhead Control Entry
summary: Crackhead Control Entry reinforces the Mission Control clinch by raising the second leg behind the opponent's head while the bottom player keeps the high-leg connection.
description: Crackhead Control Entry reinforces the Mission Control clinch by raising the second leg behind the opponent's head while the bottom player keeps the high-leg connection.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in Rubber Guard with Mission Control established, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. The opponent still faces the guard player. Both arms may remain inside; this does not automatically complete Dead Orchard or Invisible Collar.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

attacker.description: Crackhead Control Entry (attacker): Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
attacker.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in Rubber Guard with Mission Control established, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. The opponent still faces the guard player. Both arms may remain inside; this does not automatically complete Dead Orchard or Invisible Collar.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees. Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again. Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The two-leg clinch preserves posture control while you select a real submission entry such as a separately established arm isolation. If the partner frees the upper body, protect the space beside your ribs with an inside frame against chest pressure before returning to ordinary guard.

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): What connection comes before the second leg rises?
flashcards.answer: Establish the first supported high leg and broken posture before bringing up the reinforcing leg.

plausible: Feet crossed low behind the waist
Unsupported foot beside the head
trap: High shin with their torso far away

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): Where does the reinforcing leg go?
flashcards.answer: The second leg rises behind the head to reinforce the facing upper-body clinch.

plausible: Across upper arm below the shoulder
On the hip beneath their elbow

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): What extra feature would identify Dead Orchard?
flashcards.answer: High legs alone do not complete Dead Orchard; confirm the both-arm leg figure-four separately.

plausible: Two high legs without a leg closure
One wrist on the mat and covered
trap: One shin held behind the head

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): What supplies the angle for comfortable high-leg control?
flashcards.answer: Use hip positioning and a connected knee rather than forcing the foot against a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip angle bringing the knee close

plausible: Pull foot while the knee stays fixed
Flat hips with the knee drifting out
trap: Raise foot without bringing hips in

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): How can you return to one-leg control?
flashcards.answer: Keep the original high shin supported while lowering the second leg to return toward Mission Control.
flashcards.answer_line: Second leg down; first shin held

plausible: Release first shin; keep legs high
Lower both legs before gripping shin
trap: First leg low; second stays high

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): The opponent folds your upper back; how do you reset?
flashcards.answer: Release the high clinch and recover frames when the upper back is compressed or the position becomes uncomfortable.

plausible: Keep feet linked and push the chest
Lower one leg; keep head pulled down
trap: Shift hips under the closed clinch

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): What must the opponent's posture allow at entry?
flashcards.answer: The entry starts from broken posture and a supported Mission Control connection, not a distant upright opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and shoulders by supported knee

plausible: Upright torso beyond the raised knee
Head close but shoulders drawn back
trap: Shoulders close but high knee wide

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): How do you check arm isolation after adding the second leg?
flashcards.answer: The second leg reinforces posture control; it does not by itself prove New York isolation or a completed both-arm triangle.
flashcards.answer_line: Locate both elbows by the high legs

plausible: Check only feet above the head
Check only head height below knee
trap: Check only that the legs touch

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): Your foot rises but the knee twists; what should change?
flashcards.answer: Stop the foot pull when the knee is fixed or twisting; use a comfortable hip angle or abandon the entry.
flashcards.answer_line: Stop foot pull; reposition the hip

plausible: Pull foot higher to close the legs
Keep knee planted; move ankle inward
trap: Let go briefly; keep knee wedged

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (bottom): After losing the high clinch, what protects your ribs?
flashcards.answer: If the opponent frees the upper body, frame inside against chest pressure and rebuild ordinary guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside forearm as the knees recover

plausible: Both hands chasing their head
Both legs high without chest contact

defender.name: Crackhead Control Entry Defender
defender.description: Crackhead Control Entry (defender): Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
defender.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in Rubber Guard with Mission Control established, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. The opponent still faces the guard player. Both arms may remain inside; this does not automatically complete Dead Orchard or Invisible Collar.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.

Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm. Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck. Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The early escape keeps an elbow inside before both legs close high. Once an arm is isolated for a submission, stop treating the exchange as a posture contest: open the controlling connection or tap before trying to lift the head.
key_principles: Keep the elbows compact: Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated.
Recognize the reinforcement: A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
Control the hip line early: Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.
Clear the upper enclosure: Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm.
Keep a safe spine: Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck.
Pass after release: Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (top): Which elbow position limits easy arm isolation?
flashcards.answer: Avoid straightening an arm between the high legs; keep the elbow compact while responding to the entry.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow bent by ribs inside the guard

plausible: Straight arm between the high legs
Elbow wide with wrist still pinned

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (top): What does the second high leg add to the first shin grip?
flashcards.answer: Recognize the second leg as reinforcement of upper-body posture control before trying to lift.

plausible: Both wrists pinned to the chest
Both extended elbows fully trapped
trap: One arm held; other shoulder free

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (top): When can a hip or thigh frame interrupt the second-leg climb?
flashcards.answer: An early hip or thigh frame with balanced base can preserve space before the high clinch closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Before legs close over the shoulders

plausible: After legs close over the shoulders
After the high legs isolate an arm
trap: Once stacking has folded their neck

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (top): What precedes standing tall or extracting an arm?
flashcards.answer: Clear the high enclosure before posture recovery or arm extraction; do not pull against a retained shoulder connection.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the high legs at the shoulders

plausible: Uncross only waist-level ankles
Lift only the chin above a foot
trap: Step only one foot farther back

flashcards.question: Crackhead Control Entry (top): What can forward stacking do while the high clinch stays closed?
flashcards.answer: Do not use a neck stack to answer the high clinch. Address the upper-body connection with balanced control.
flashcards.answer_line: Load their neck; shoulders stay held

plausible: Fold slides the high leg below elbow
Stack frees shoulders from knee hug
trap: Head pressure opens the high legs
